study type: Retrospective analysis of a prospectively recruited cohort
exposure: Labor induction at different gestational weeks
Gestational age at delivery (37 weeks, 38 weeks, 39 weeks, 40 weeks, 41 weeks)
outcome: Composite adverse neonatal outcomes (neonatal hypoglycemia, phototherapy, clavicle fracture, umbilical artery pH < 7.15)
cohort: 797 singleton pregnancies complicated by diet-controlled gestational diabetes mellitus, diagnosed, treated, and delivered after 37 weeks in a tertiary, university-affiliated perinatal center between January 2016 and December 2021
finding: The lowest rate of neonatal complications was observed at 40 weeks gestation.
mod_finding: Labor induction at 40 weeks was associated with a decreased risk of fetal macrosomia compared to expectant management.
